fields.label: Panels ×8
rows: Ethylene propylene diene rubber, and the default for a grommet that sees weather, water, steam or coolant. Excellent ozone and UV resistance, so it holds an outdoor or engine-bay aperture for years without hardening at the lip. Not for petroleum oils.

Nitrile butadiene rubber, the general-purpose industry standard. Outstanding resistance to petroleum oils and hydraulic fluids at moderate temperature — the choice for a grommet on the oil side of a housing or gearbox.

Polychloroprene. The compound most grommet enquiries settle on, because it takes weather, ozone and moderate oil at the same time — the condition an exposed panel aperture actually lives in. Also the family we reach for when flame retardancy is specified.

Vinyl methyl silicone, the widest service range of the eight. Specified for grommets at hot apertures and in lighting, oven and appliance panels. Biocompatible and food-contact grades on request. Poor abrasion resistance — not for a cable that moves against the bore.

Ethylene acrylic elastomer. Our signature compound, supplied to Mahindra & Mahindra for engine and transmission applications. Specified for a bulkhead or engine-bay grommet where oil, heat and ozone act together and neither EPDM nor nitrile will hold.

Fluorocarbon rubber, the first choice for aggressive chemical environments. Resists petroleum oils, fuels and many solvents at sustained high temperature. On a grommet it is a specialist answer — specify it when the aperture is in a chemical or fuel environment, not as a default.
Styrene butadiene rubber. Abrasion resistance at low cost, for grommets in water and mild service where the part protects a cable edge rather than seals an environment. Not for oil or fuel contact.

Polyisoprene. The highest resilience of the eight, so it grips a panel groove hard and keeps gripping — useful on a grommet that has to stay put through vibration. Not for oil, fuel or sustained heat.
fields.note: Eight panels. EPDM leads because a grommet is usually about environment rather than chemistry, and neoprene is third and absent from the live page entirely despite being where most grommet enquiries land. FKM moves down to sixth with an explicit note that it is a specialist answer here. Every range matches the homepage compound table, which governs across all eleven category pages.
